summary: Closed the last discriminator the NoSnapshot snapshot-call question carried, by source instead of by another run, and rewrote that question's account as a successor with the same conclusion and defect claim. The handler-side branch - a forwarded Compaction::Snapshot unwinding inside a peer's message handling - is reachable only if a peer can produce that message for a NoSnapshot receiver, and it cannot: all nodes of one cluster instantiate SequencePaxos over the same entry type, the sender of a Snapshot compaction is the node whose own snapshot call runs first, and that call panics on a NoSnapshot instance before the forwarding loop runs, so no NoSnapshot node is ever sent one from a peer of its own cluster. Reaching that branch would need a sender outside the shared entry type, which no legal configuration provides; the reachable failure mode stays the caller-initiated public call, witnessed on a drifted leader (2cb2a3f1e43b4942b5bb3f42bad11091 event 129) and on a healthy, never-re-synchronized cluster (0b9c22ae5fb043588aa7efa3ad009b25 event 241, with the three nodes consistent at accepted 6 / decided 6 and a six-element decided log before and after). The account's counterevidence and limitations now separate the two branches and state what the closure rests on. No execution was requested and nothing was run, so the run ends with the audit in a coherent state: the parent drift account (violated, defect asserted, six consequence classes over ten receipts, gaps 3 and 5 answered), the trim child (violated, with its gap split into a source-closed in-cluster half and an open storage-level half), the snapshot child (violated, lagging-replica variant executed, peer-side still derived), the explained leader-election child, and the NoSnapshot question explained with both witnesses. What remains is only what needs new harness work: the storage-level routes below a compacted index, the forwarded-compaction peer sampling, and a delivered Snapshot compaction to a NoSnapshot instance.
